story_description: Establish foundational communication layer between Blaze and the Codex app-server daemon, enabling JSON-RPC based interaction for advanced scenarios where the app-server mode provides better session management and event streaming than direct CLI invocation.
task_description: Create CodexAppServerEvents module responsible for parsing the Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream from the Codex app-server daemon, normalizing raw events into the NormalizedEvent type consumed by the UI layer, and handling stream lifecycle including reconnection state and buffering.
atom_description: Implement CodexAppServerEvents actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerEvents.swift providing comprehensive SSE stream parsing for the Codex app-server notification channel. The module receives raw SSE data lines from the adapter layer, parses event type and data fields per SSE specification, deserializes JSON payloads into strongly-typed Codex event structs, maps Codex-specific event types to the shared NormalizedEvent enum for UI consumption, handles malformed events gracefully with logging, manages event buffering during reconnection, and exposes an AsyncSequence-based API for downstream consumers. Supports all Codex app-server event types including prompt_started, token_generated, tool_call_started, tool_call_completed, error_occurred, and session_ended.
problem_statement: The Codex app-server emits real-time events via Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream to notify clients of ongoing activity such as token generation, tool invocations, and errors. The raw SSE stream contains untyped JSON payloads with Codex-specific field names and structures that differ from our unified NormalizedEvent schema used by the UI layer. Without a dedicated parsing and normalization layer, the adapter would need to embed parsing logic, the UI would need Codex-specific handling, and error recovery would be inconsistent. We need a focused event stream parser that translates the raw SSE stream into a clean AsyncSequence of NormalizedEvents that the rest of the application can consume uniformly.

All event data payloads are valid JSON objects
Codex event types are stable and documented in Codex CLI source or documentation
Event timestamps use Unix epoch milliseconds as integer values
Events are ordered chronologically by server emission time
Maximum event payload size is under 1MB
Reconnection with Last-Event-ID header is supported by app-server

Swift AsyncSequence backpressure is sufficient for expected event rates
constraints: Must use Swift Concurrency with actor isolation for thread safety
No third-party SSE parsing libraries allowed (use custom parser)
Event parsing must not block the main thread
Must handle incomplete events gracefully during stream interruption
Memory usage for buffered events must not exceed 10MB
Event normalization must preserve all information needed by UI
Must log all parsing errors at warning level for debugging
Parser must be stateless between events (no cross-event dependencies except buffering)
Must support cancellation via Task cancellation propagation
All public types must be Sendable for cross-actor usage

CodexAppServerEvents.feed(line: String) async - processes single SSE line and potentially yields events
CodexAppServerEvents.eventStream: AsyncStream<NormalizedEvent> - stream of normalized events for consumption
CodexAppServerEvents.stateStream: AsyncStream<StreamState> - stream of state changes for monitoring
CodexAppServerEvents.lastEventId: String? - last received event ID for reconnection header

event_contracts: NormalizedEvent.promptStarted - emitted when Codex begins processing a prompt with prompt_id and model
NormalizedEvent.assistantDelta - emitted for each token with content string and is_final flag
NormalizedEvent.toolCallStarted - emitted when Codex invokes a tool with tool_name and arguments
NormalizedEvent.toolCallCompleted - emitted when tool execution finishes with result and duration
NormalizedEvent.error - emitted on Codex error with code, message, and recoverable flag
NormalizedEvent.sessionEnded - emitted when Codex session terminates with reason and stats
StreamState.connected - emitted when SSE connection established and events flowing
StreamState.disconnected - emitted when SSE connection lost
StreamState.reconnecting - emitted when attempting to reconnect with buffering active
StreamState.error(Error) - emitted on unrecoverable stream error
edge_cases: EC-01: Empty data field in SSE event - skip event with debug log, do not yield
EC-02: Missing event type field - default to message type per SSE spec
EC-03: Malformed JSON in data field - log warning with first 200 chars of data, skip event
EC-04: Unknown event type string - parse as unknown(String) variant, normalize to generic event
EC-05: Event ID with special characters - store as-is for reconnection header
EC-06: Retry field present - log but ignore (retry logic in adapter layer)
EC-07: Very large data field over 1MB - attempt parse, may fail with memory error, skip
EC-08: Data split across multiple data: lines - accumulate correctly with newlines preserved
EC-09: Rapid event burst over 1000/sec - apply backpressure via AsyncStream buffer
EC-10: Consumer slower than producer - AsyncStream buffers, may drop if buffer limit policy set
EC-11: Stream interrupted mid-event - discard incomplete pending data on reset
EC-12: Empty line before any data - ignore, do not emit empty event
EC-13: Comment lines interspersed - skip comment lines, continue accumulation
EC-14: Timestamp in future - clamp to current time with warning
EC-15: Timestamp is zero - use current time as fallback with warning
EC-16: Tool arguments contain nested JSON - AnyCodable preserves structure correctly
failure_modes: FM-01: JSON decode failure - log warning with event type and error, skip event, continue processing
FM-02: Unknown event type - normalize to generic NormalizedEvent.unknown variant, log info
FM-03: Buffer overflow during extended reconnection - drop oldest events, log warning with count dropped
FM-04: Continuation already finished - check before yield, log error if attempting to yield to finished stream
FM-05: Actor reentrancy during rapid feed() calls - actor isolation prevents, but log if detected
FM-06: Memory pressure from large events - rely on system memory warnings, no custom handling
FM-07: Invalid UTF-8 in SSE line - String initializer handles, log warning if lossy conversion
FM-08: Extremely long line without newline - URLSession line reading handles, may split
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerEvents.swift and Tests/Engine/CodexAppServerEventsTests.swift. Remove imports from CodexAppServerAdapter.swift. The parser is stateless code with no persistent data, so removal is clean. Events already processed and persisted to SessionStore remain unaffected.

notes: This parser is focused on correctness and robustness over performance. The SSE format is simple but has edge cases around multi-line data and comment handling. The W3C spec is the authoritative reference. Consider extracting generic SSEParser if needed for other providers. The normalization layer is critical for UI consistency across Claude, Gemini, and Codex engines.

risks: Codex event payload schema may differ from assumptions requiring parser updates
SSE specification edge cases may not be correctly handled in initial implementation
High event throughput could cause backpressure issues with AsyncStream
Memory usage could spike if many large events buffered during extended reconnection
Event normalization may lose information needed by UI requiring schema expansion
mitigations: Define payload structs with optional fields to handle schema variations gracefully
Reference W3C SSE spec directly and add comprehensive unit tests for edge cases
Use AsyncStream buffer policy to handle backpressure and log if events dropped
Implement buffer size limit with configurable max and drop-oldest policy
Design NormalizedEvent with extensible associated values to add fields without breaking changes
risk_register.blast_radius: Low - parser is isolated module used only by CodexAppServerAdapter. Failure causes Codex event display issues but does not affect Claude or Gemini engines. No data persistence affected since parser is stateless.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If SSE parser proves problematic, fall back to raw JSON line parsing without SSE framing (if Codex supports NDJSON mode). Alternatively, disable real-time event display and poll for session state instead.
